blocking.section: Cutover runbook / Stage 4 shadow traffic; Rollback
blocking.issue: The shadow exit criteria and the authentication trigger cannot be measured with the mechanisms the runbook prescribes. (a) Ruralz responses are discarded and the comparison uses aggregate per-Route metrics, so no one can compute "agreement for 99.9% of mirrored requests" or explain each disagreement. That needs requests paired with their outcomes on both gateways, and the runbook names no source for KrakenD's per-path status codes. (b) Rule 1 mirrors only safe methods, so a Route that serves only `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` never receives shadow data. Its per-Route exit gate is then undefined. These are the Routes with body validation, transforms and holds. (c) During a split each request reaches only one gateway, so "a Route where KrakenD admitted the same client" cannot be observed. Operators cannot run Stage 4 or the Rollback table as written.
blocking.evidence: Line 732: "Mirror production requests to Ruralz Gateway and discard its responses"; line 739: "Mirror only safe methods (`GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`)."; line 742: "Compare per Route, from metrics ... against KrakenD's status codes"; line 743: "status classes agree for 99.9% or more of mirrored requests per Route (target), every disagreement is explained by an accepted report item"; line 762: "Any `RZ-AUTH` rejection on a Route where KrakenD admitted the same client".
blocking.fix: Define how requests are paired. The load balancer or ingress stamps a request ID header on both copies. Both gateways log it: Ruralz in its access log, KrakenD through `telemetry/logging` or OpenTelemetry. A join of the two logs gives per-request status-class agreement. Say where KrakenD's per-path status counts come from. For Routes that serve only unsafe methods, state the alternative gate: Stage 2 cases against non-production Upstreams, mirroring to non-production copies, or entry at the 1% split step with a closer watch. Restate the authentication trigger for the split as a comparison of per-Route `RZ-AUTH` 401 and 403 rates against KrakenD's 401 and 403 rates over the same window, with a tagged threshold (target).

blocking.section: Cutover runbook / Stage 4 shadow traffic (KrakenD's own traffic shadowing)
blocking.issue: The second mirroring option does not produce comparable traffic. A KrakenD shadow backend is a backend: it receives the request KrakenD builds for its backends. That request uses the backend's own `url_pattern` path and carries only the headers and query strings that `input_headers` and `input_query_strings` allow, which is none by default. Pointed at Ruralz Gateway, it sends paths that match no imported Route and requests without `Authorization`. Every mirrored request then diverges. Allowlisting headers on the endpoint to fix that also changes what production backends receive. It is also defined per backend, so an aggregating endpoint needs one added shadow backend per path.
blocking.evidence: Line 735: "**KrakenD's own traffic shadowing**, offered in both editions ... through a shadow backend (`proxy` `shadow` at backend scope ...) that points at Ruralz Gateway." Research section 3: `input_headers` "No client headers are forwarded by default"; section 4: `url_pattern` "Path only, with no scheme or host".
blocking.fix: Either remove this option, or state its constraints. Each shadowed endpoint needs a shadow backend whose `url_pattern` equals the endpoint path and whose host is Ruralz Gateway. The endpoint's `input_headers` and `input_query_strings` must list every parameter Ruralz Policies read, and this changes what production backends receive. Aggregating endpoints are mirrored once, not once per backend. Recommend the load balancer mirror as the only supported option when these constraints cannot be met.

blocking.issue: The ordered steps miss the move from the shadow State Store to the production State Store. Stage 4 puts shadow Nodes on their own State Store. Stage 5 then shifts client traffic to those Nodes with no step that repoints them or resets shadow counters. Stage 6 deletes "the shadow State Store". The URL is a `secretRef` resolved per Node, typically from `RURALZ_STATE_STORE_URL` with `provider: env`. Changing it means a Node restart or a new Revision, which neither Stage 5 nor the Gate summary contains. Followed literally, production traffic runs against the shadow store with counters inflated by mirrored traffic until Stage 6 removes it.
blocking.evidence: Line 740: "Run shadow Nodes on their own State Store, so mirrored requests never consume production Quotas, Rate Limits or Token Budgets that Stage 5 uses."; line 776: "Remove any KrakenD shadow backend configuration and the shadow State Store."; Gate summary line 788: "| 5 Side-by-side cutover | Shadow exit | 100% weight baked, no trigger (target) |" with no State Store step.
blocking.fix: Add a Stage 5 step 0: repoint the Nodes' State Store secret to the production State Store and restart or Hot Reload them. Say which one the `secretRef` provider requires. Confirm readiness and the digest, and only then raise the weight above 0. Or run separate shadow Nodes and a separate cutover Node set. Add the step to the Gate summary entry gate for Stage 5.

blocking.issue: `propagate_claims` is endpoint-scoped, but it maps to an Upstream-scoped `headers` Policy. The importer shares one Upstream among all backends with the same hosts and backend-scope namespaces, and endpoint namespaces are not part of that key. The Policy therefore also runs on Routes that do no JWT validation. On those Routes `auth` is null, so `auth.claims` raises a CEL runtime error. `headers` defaults to `failureMode: closed`, so those Routes fail with 503. The `equivalent` level hides a failure on unrelated Routes.
blocking.evidence: Line 179: "| `auth/validator` `propagate_claims` | E | Upstream-scoped `headers` Policy with `request.set[].valueExpression` over `auth.claims` | `equivalent` |"; line 127: "one `Upstream` per distinct combination of host list, service discovery settings, TLS and backend-scope namespaces, so backends that share a host share an Upstream"; Configuration model variables: `auth` "null before auth"; registry: `headers` "closed; either"; `valueExpression` runtime error: "Policy `failureMode`".
blocking.fix: Map `propagate_claims` to a Route-scoped `headers` Policy (`request.set[]` runs at onRequestHeaders at Route scope), or guard it with `when: 'auth != null'`. Alternatively, add endpoint-scope claim propagation to the Upstream dedup key. Keep `equivalent` only after that change.
